2025 Outlook in the European Technology Ecosystem

According to data from the Europe & Turkey Technology and Investment Report, Europe-based technology companies received a total of 72 billion euros in investment in 2025. This figure was recorded as the second-highest investment volume of the last three years. While more than 3,740 deals were completed throughout the year, investor interest was observed to shift especially toward infrastructure technologies that provide economic resilience, industrial competitiveness, and long-term growth.

In funding rounds, AI, data center infrastructures, and renewable energy solutions were the standout sectors. The increase in strategic and infrastructure-focused investments indicates that the ecosystem is maturing.

25 Technology Companies Receiving the Highest Investment

Below are the companies ranked by the amount of funding they received in 2025 and their fields of activity:

  • CityFibre (UK) – 2.3 Billion Pounds: Fiber-to-the-premises (FTTP) infrastructure provider.
  • Propel Finance (UK) – 1.5 Billion Pounds: Asset and vehicle financing solutions for businesses.
  • Mistral AI (France) – 1.7 Billion Euros: Open-source large language models (LLM) and generative AI tools.
  • Nscale (UK) – 1.53 Billion Dollars: High-performance GPU-powered AI cloud and data center infrastructure.
  • Ubisoft (France) – 1.16 Billion Euros: Game development and digital entertainment publishing.
  • Bending Spoons (Italy) – 1.1 Billion Euros: Digital product development and software scaling platform.
  • EcoDataCenter (Sweden) – 1.05 Billion Euros: Sustainable and high-performance data centers.
  • Finn (Germany) – 1 Billion Euros: Subscription-based vehicle ownership platform.
  • NXP Semiconductors (Netherlands) – 1 Billion Euros: Automotive and IoT-focused semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Grammarly (Ukraine) – 1 Billion Dollars: AI-powered writing assistant and communication platform.
  • Nebius (Netherlands) – 1 Billion Dollars: Full-stack AI cloud infrastructure and GPU clusters.
  • Nokia (Finland) – 1 Billion Dollars: Network infrastructure and telecommunications technologies (focused on AI integration).
  • Enpal (Germany) – 810 Million Euros: Solar energy and integrated home energy management solutions.
  • Your.World (Netherlands) – 800 Million Euros: Online services and digital transformation solutions.
  • Oura (Finland) – 900 Million Dollars: Smart health tracking ring and biometric data analytics.
  • Helsing (Germany) – 600 Million Euros: AI-based software solutions for the defense industry.
  • IONITY (Germany) – 600 Million Euros: High-power electric vehicle charging network.
  • Capital on Tap (UK) – 500 Million Pounds: Credit and financing platform for SMEs.
  • Isomorphic Labs (UK) – 600 Million Dollars: AI models for drug discovery.
  • Bees & Bears (Germany) – 505 Million Euros: Embedded finance platform for renewable energy products.
  • Brevo (France) – 500 Million Euros: CRM and omnichannel marketing automation.
  • Elvy (Sweden) – 500 Million Euros: Energy management and optimization software.
  • Lovable (Sweden) – 470 Million Euros: No-code application development platform powered by natural language processing.
  • Ferovinum (UK) – 400 Million Pounds: Supply chain financing for the wine and beverage industry.
  • Electra (France) – 433 Million Euros: Fast-charging station operation for electric vehicles.
